                         MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION OF
                  NORTHERN VIRGINIA ELECTRIC COOPERATIVE, INC.

         Pursuant to Rule 212 of the Rules of Practice and Procedure of the Federal Energy

Regulatory Commission (“FERC” or the “Commission”),1 Northern Virginia Electric

Cooperative, Inc. (“NOVEC”) respectfully submits this motion for clarification of the

Commission’s June 18, 2026 Order on Rehearing, Clarification, Compliance Filing, and Paper

Hearing on PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (“PJM”) (“Order”) in these consolidated dockets.2

NOVEC seeks clarification regarding the nature of the information that the Commission

contemplates needing in order to determine whether to approve a charge to reflect the reliance on

and benefit from the transmission system of Eligible Customers serving Eligible Load but

                                                         2
 electing to take a de minimis amount of, or not reserve any, transmission service. NOVEC seeks

such clarification because, as explained in the Request for Rehearing and Clarification of the

Indicated PJM Indicated Transmission Owners,3 the PJM Transmission Owners submitted

extensive evidence explaining the need for and derivation of the proposed charge. The

Commission’s rejection of the proposal without any explanation of what the Commission found

wanting makes it difficult to discern what the Commission feels it needs that was not already

provided to it.

                                          I.      BACKGROUND

        In response to the Commission’s December 18, 2025, order establishing a paper hearing

to determine the rates, terms, and conditions for the new transmission services for Eligible

Customers serving Co-Located Load,4 the PJM Transmission Owners proposed that Eligible

Customers serving Co-Located Load pay a Grid Reliance Charge “based on the difference

between the amount of their firm contract demand for Firm Contract Demand Service or, in the

case of Non-Firm Contract Demand Service customers, the amount of their reserved service, and

their total (gross) on-site load.”5 This charge reflected the fact that, “[e]ven with a zero MW

contract demand, a large Co-Located Load and generation arrangement will still depend on the

grid for the delivery of various ancillary services and a suite of synchronization support services,

such as stable frequency, inertia, stability services (damping, angle stability), fault current

capability, and ride-through and protection coordination.”6

         NOVEC supports the concept of the proposed Grid Reliance Charge. A charge of this

nature is necessary to complement the Commission’s correct finding that all Eligible Customers

taking a new transmission service on behalf of Co-Located Load need to be assessed charges for

regulation and black start services on a gross demand basis.7 Neither black start nor regulation

services include a component for transmission delivery in the computation of the rates charged

for those services, but network customers are already paying a transmission charge based on

their total load.8 Any customer using black start and regulation services (or any other

transmission-dependent service) without otherwise procuring transmission service covering its

total load (including nameplate capacity of the generator) would be using the transmission

system as a free rider that is not contributing to the costs of maintaining and operating the

transmission system and hence is being subsidized by other transmission customers.

        Despite the inevitability of subsidization without an additional charge, the Commission

concluded in the Order that the “that record…does not adequately substantiate the need for an

additional charge at this time or how such a charge should be calculated and assessed.”9 The

Commission further stated that “the new transmission services created in this proceeding could

raise novel questions regarding application of cost causation principles” and “experience with the

actual use of these new transmission services will improve our understanding of any potential

issues and inform whether future action [on an additional charge] is needed.”10 As such, the

Commission welcomed future section 205 or 206 filings on additional charges or a version of the

                            II.     MOTION FOR CLARIFICATION

           NOVEC respectfully disagrees that the record does not substantiate the need for an

additional charge, and it is not clear what additional support the Commission believes it would

have needed to support approval of a rate akin to or serving the purpose of the proposed Grid

Reliance Charge. NOVEC did not seek rehearing on this issue because NOVEC expects that the

PJM stakeholder process will result in submission of another proposal for the Commission’s

consideration, particularly if the Commission provides clarification regarding the nature of the

additional information the Commission thinks it would need to have before it in order to support

an additional charge if it does not grant the PJM Transmission Owners’ Request for Rehearing

on this issue.

           NOVEC is not asking the Commission to prejudge any future filing. Establishing the

need for a charge and then supporting the associated rate and rate design are necessary elements

of any such filing. But the Commission’s ruling is ambiguous because there is no dispute that the

PJM rates for black start and regulation services do not include any costs or components for

transmission service, and it is undeniable that transmission service is necessary in order for black

start or regulation service to be provided and used. It is equally clear that the transmission system

supports Co-Located Loads through synchronization services and that even the option to use the

transmission system as a backup has value since generators cannot be online all the time. Large

loads have consistently expressed interest in the additional reliability benefits that come from



11
     Id.

                                                   5
 interconnection with the transmission system.12 Other than cost support13 for the rate itself, it is

not clear what other evidence the Commission could expect to see or need to support the need for

such a charge, and the Commission provided no such guidance in the Order. NOVEC thus seeks

clarification to assist the development of appropriate proposals in the stakeholder process if the

Commission does not grant the PJM Transmission Owners’ Request for Rehearing on this issue.

         The Commission also suggested that “experience with the actual use” of the new

transmission services would help support its understanding.14 NOVEC requests that the

Commission clarify that it would consider a section 205 proposal before Co-Located Load

begins operating in PJM if it does not grant the PJM Transmission Owners’ Request for

Rehearing on this issue. Although the effective date is a matter for a further compliance filing,

there is at least the possibility that the new transmission services will not be offered for some

time, perhaps several years. NOVEC submits that stakeholders should work on and file an

alternative proposal in the meantime without waiting to develop specific experience with the

actual provision of the service. As stated above, if Co-Located Load is permitted to begin

operating before a transmission service charge such as the Grid Reliance Charge is in place, Co-

Located Load will be subsidized by other transmission customers. NOVEC accordingly requests

that the Commission clarify that it is not requiring actual experience with the new transmission

                                   III.    CONCLUSION

       WHEREFORE, for the foregoing reasons, NOVEC respectfully requests that the

Commission issue an order clarifying the Order as requested herein.
